title: Sanger Tree of Life Sample Homogenisation: Cryogenic Bead Beating of Samples
author: Benjamin Jackson
materials: Prepare all necessary equipment prior to starting and place any applicable items (e.g. cold blocks, tools) onto dry ice.

steps.title: Prepare Tubes and Beads
steps.instruction: Add the required number and type of beads (refer to Table 1 in Guidelines) to the appropriate tubes and place them in a cold block on dry ice. Alternatively, pre-chill beads before adding them after the sample.

steps.title: Add and Prepare Tissue Samples
steps.instruction: Weigh the required amount of whole-frozen tissue on dry ice and transfer it into the pre-chilled tubes containing beads, ensuring tissues remain under cryogenic conditions to avoid freeze/thaw cycles.

substeps.instruction: Dissect tissue into pieces < 1 cm² if required using scissors, a scalpel, or by crushing.
For hard corals, use a cold sterile pestle and mortar if necessary to break pieces.
For recalcitrant tissue types (see Guidelines), dissect into pieces < 5 mm² and manually interrupt structures by crushing.

steps.title: Load Samples into FluidX Racks
steps.instruction: Transfer all tubes to either a FluidX 48-rack or a FluidX 24-rack on dry ice and securely fit the lid.

substeps.instruction: For 1.9 mL or 1.0 mL FluidX tubes: process up to 96 samples using two FluidX 48-racks.
For 4 mL vials: process up to 48 samples using two FluidX 24-racks.
If using only one rack, prepare a second rack with an equal number of empty FluidX tubes to balance the FastPrep®-96.

steps.title: Cryogenic Equilibration
steps.instruction: Submerge the FluidX rack(s) in liquid nitrogen while wearing appropriate PPE until the temperature equilibrates (bubbling stops, approximately 15 seconds).

steps.title: Load FastPrep®-96
steps.instruction: Remove the rack from liquid nitrogen with tongs, drain remaining liquid, and place back on dry ice.

substeps.instruction: Remove the FluidX rack lid.
Place the rack onto the FastPrep®-96.
Fit the top adapter directly on top of the sample tubes and fasten tightly.

steps.title: Homogenise Samples
steps.instruction: Homogenise the frozen samples on the FastPrep®-96 using the time and speed specified for the sample type (refer to Table 1 in Guidelines).

steps.title: Post-Homogenisation Cooling
steps.instruction: Remove the rack from the FastPrep®-96, place it on dry ice, and securely fit the lid.

substeps.instruction: Resubmerge the rack in liquid nitrogen until temperature equilibrates (bubbling stops, ~15 seconds).

steps.title: Iterative Disruption and Inspection
steps.instruction: Repeat the loading, homogenisation, and cooling steps (steps 5 to 8) as required by the sample type until tissues are a fine powder.

substeps.instruction: Manually inspect novel specimens after disruptions.
Manually inspect isopod, amphipod, and decapod samples after the first disruption to determine if a second is needed.
For plant samples: repeat steps 6 to 8 up to 6 times total. If still not disrupted, use an alternative specimen/tissue type or bead type (e.g., 2 x 3 mm tungsten carbide beads).
For hard corals that will not disrupt: empty the vial onto a sterile, cold weighing boat on dry ice, use sterile forceps to place undisrupted chunks back into the 4 mL vial, and repeat bead beating.
Note: Liquid nitrogen submersion is optional after the final disruption to prevent thawing.

steps.title: Final Stabilization
steps.instruction: Place the FluidX rack(s) on dry ice for > 3 minutes to ensure all disrupted tissue remains frozen.

steps.title: Sample Recovery and Storage
steps.instruction: Proceed to downstream procedures or store disrupted tissues long term at –70°C (do not thaw prior to use).

substeps.instruction: For 4 mL vials: decant disrupted tissue onto clean cold weighing boats on dry ice using sterile tools, recooling the tube if necessary.
For hard corals: reweigh disrupted tissue to ensure adequate weight and transfer to a new tube (e.g., FluidX or microcentrifuge tube).
For DNA/RNA extraction of corals: the zirconium oxide bead can be transferred to the new tube to retain tissue.

steps.title: Bead Removal for Downstream Processing
steps.instruction: Remove specific beads from tubes prior to downstream processing based on sample and application.

substeps.instruction: Plants, fungi, chordates, and arthropods (including isopods, amphipods, and decapods): remove stainless steel or tungsten carbide beads.
Bryophytes for RNA extraction: remove stainless steel beads.
Bryophytes for DNA extraction: 5/32” zirconium oxide beads may remain in the tube.
